questions.question: When a document is uploaded, an indexing service, a billing service, and an audit service must each receive and process their own copy of the same message. Which Azure Service Bus design should you use?

options.text: One topic with a separate subscription for each service
options.why: Correct. A topic copies each message to every subscription, and each service reads from its own subscription.

options.text: One queue with three competing receivers
options.why: Competing receivers on a queue share the messages, so each message reaches only one service.

options.text: One queue with sessions enabled
options.why: Sessions provide ordered processing of related messages. They do not copy a message to several consumers.

options.text: A Basic tier namespace with three queues and one sender per queue
options.why: This forces the sender to know every consumer. A topic decouples the sender from the consumers.

questions.explanation: Topics and subscriptions implement publish and subscribe. New consumers can be added as new subscriptions without changing the sender.

questions.scenario: A subscription named billing must receive only messages that have an application property named tier with the value premium. Message throughput is high, and filter evaluation must have the lowest possible overhead.
questions.question: Which type of rule should you add to the billing subscription?

options.text: A correlation filter that matches tier equal to premium
options.why: Correct. Correlation filters match exact property values and are more efficient to evaluate than SQL filters.

options.text: A SQL filter with the expression tier LIKE '%prem%'
options.why: This works, but a LIKE expression is evaluated as SQL and has higher overhead than an exact correlation match.

options.text: A true filter
options.why: A true filter accepts every message, so non-premium messages would also be received.

options.text: A false filter
options.why: A false filter accepts no messages.

questions.explanation: Use correlation filters for exact-match conditions on system or application properties. Use SQL filters when comparisons or pattern matching are required.

questions.question: You add a SQL filter rule named PremiumOnly to an existing subscription. The subscription continues to receive every message published to the topic. What should you do?

options.text: Delete the $Default rule from the subscription
options.why: Correct. The $Default rule is a true filter. A message is copied to the subscription if any rule matches.

options.text: Increase the maximum delivery count of the subscription
options.why: The maximum delivery count controls dead-lettering after failed deliveries. It does not affect filtering.

options.text: Enable duplicate detection on the topic
options.why: Duplicate detection removes repeated sends. It does not filter messages by property.

options.text: Enable sessions on the subscription
options.why: Sessions control ordered processing. They do not change which messages match the subscription.

questions.explanation: Every new subscription has a $Default rule that accepts all messages. Remove it when you add a more selective filter.

questions.question: A Python support tool must read messages that were moved from the queue named jobs after they exceeded the maximum delivery count. How should the tool create its receiver?

options.text: client.get_queue_receiver(queue_name="jobs", sub_queue=ServiceBusSubQueue.DEAD_LETTER)
options.why: Correct. The sub_queue parameter opens the dead-letter queue of the jobs queue.

options.text: client.get_queue_receiver(queue_name="jobs", receive_mode=ServiceBusReceiveMode.RECEIVE_AND_DELETE)
options.why: This reads the main queue, not the dead-letter queue, and removes messages on delivery.

options.text: client.get_queue_receiver(queue_name="jobs", session_id="deadletter")
options.why: A session ID selects a session in a session-enabled queue. It does not open the dead-letter queue.

options.text: client.get_topic_sender(topic_name="jobs")
options.why: A sender cannot receive messages, and jobs is a queue, not a topic.

questions.explanation: Each queue and subscription has a dead-letter sub-queue. In the Python SDK, pass sub_queue=ServiceBusSubQueue.DEAD_LETTER when creating the receiver.

questions.question: Which TWO conditions can cause Azure Service Bus to move a message to a dead-letter queue?

options.text: The message delivery count exceeds the maximum delivery count
options.why: Correct. The message is dead-lettered with the reason MaxDeliveryCountExceeded.

options.text: The receiving application calls dead_letter_message for the message
options.why: Correct. An application can explicitly dead-letter a message and provide a reason.

options.text: The receiving application calls complete_message for the message
options.why: Completing a message removes it permanently. It does not move it to the dead-letter queue.

options.text: The message is received in peek-lock mode
options.why: Peek-lock is the normal receive mode and does not, by itself, dead-letter a message.

questions.explanation: Messages are dead-lettered when delivery attempts are exhausted, when they expire with dead-lettering on expiration enabled, when filter evaluation fails, or when the application dead-letters them.
